social_history.occupation: Retired professional soprano, now voice coach

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert and oriented x4. Emotional about changes to her voice.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Tongue atrophy bilateral, visible fasciculations at rest. Dysarthria — nasal quality, hypophonic. Jaw jerk brisk. Palatal elevation asymmetric (right reduced).
neurological_exam.motor: Bilateral hand intrinsic weakness with wasting. Right shoulder abduction 4/5. Fasciculations visible in bilateral deltoids, triceps, and calves.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps 3+ bilaterally. Hoffmans bilateral. Bilateral Babinski positive.
neurological_exam.additional: Prominent bulbar-onset in professional singer — voice changes particularly distressing to this patient.

patient.chief_complaint: Progressive speech changes and bilateral hand weakness over 11 months
patient.history_present_illness: Mrs. V is a 64-year-old retired professional soprano and current voice coach who presents with an 11-month history of progressive dysarthria, voice changes, and bilateral hand weakness. As a professional voice user, she first noticed subtle changes in her vocal quality approximately 11 months ago, which she initially attributed to vocal fatigue or aging. Over the ensuing months, her speech became increasingly nasal and hypophonic, and she began to have difficulty sustaining high notes during her coaching sessions. She subsequently noticed progressive weakness in both hands, finding it increasingly difficult to demonstrate piano playing technique and to button her shirt. Approximately 6 months ago, her students began commenting on visible muscle twitching in her arms during lessons. Her husband noticed her tongue fasciculating approximately 4 months ago. She has no history of botulinum toxin injections to the vocal cords. Her levothyroxine dose has been stable for 3 years with consistent normal TSH. She has no dysphagia to solids but reports occasional coughing with thin liquids. She denies any cognitive changes. Her progression has been relentless and she reports marked functional decline over the past 6 months compared to her initial presentation.

findings.location: Bilateral corticospinal tracts — internal capsule, cerebral peduncles, and anterior brainstem
Bilateral cranial nerve XII nuclei (hypoglossal nuclei in dorsal medulla)

additional_observations: No mass effect on lower cranial nerves
mri.impression: Bilateral symmetric corticospinal tract T2 hyperintensity from internal capsule to brainstem, with subtle signal change in hypoglossal nuclei. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Tongue: fibrillations +2, large polyphasic MUPs (chronic denervation/reinnervation), reduced recruitment. Mentalis: fasciculations. Consistent with bulbar lower motor neuron involvement.
Bilateral FDI, APB: fibrillations +2, positive sharp waves, large MUPs (duration >14ms). Bilateral deltoids: fasciculations +1. Cervical paraspinals C5-C7: fibrillations +1.
Bilateral tibialis anterior: fasciculations. Left gastrocnemius: fibrillations +1.
Median, ulnar, sural: normal amplitude and conduction velocities throughout. No sensory neuropathy.
Median motor (bilateral): CMAP amplitudes reduced (right 3.8 mV, left 3.2 mV; reference >4.5 mV). Normal distal latencies and conduction velocities. No conduction block.

specialized_test.impression: Definite ALS, bulbar-onset with limb involvement. Widespread neurogenic changes in all four body regions. Normal sensory NCS excludes sensorimotor neuropathy. No conduction block excludes MMN.
recommended_actions: ALS confirmed. Riluzole. Swallowing evaluation. PFT. ALS MDC.

output.interpretation: Abnormal values: FVC 76 % predicted (L), FEV1 78 % predicted (L), SNIP 54 cmH2O (L), NIF -48 cmH2O (H).
abnormal_values_summary: SNIP 54 cmH2O (below 70 cmH2O threshold for women)

findings.finding: Reduced tongue base retraction with premature bolus spillage
Pharyngeal residue after thin liquid swallow
Penetration to vocal cords with thin liquids — PAS score 4
No aspiration below cords with nectar-thick liquids

output.impression: Oropharyngeal dysphagia with silent penetration on thin liquids. Recommend nectar-thick liquids and soft diet. Early PEG consideration given declining FVC.
recommended_actions: PEG tube placement consultation given FVC 76% — place before FVC falls below 50%
Refer to speech-language pathology for compensatory strategies

interactions: Levothyroxine: no direct pharmacokinetic interaction with riluzole. However, riluzole initiation may subtly affect CYP metabolism — monitor TSH at 3-month check to ensure thyroid replacement remains adequate.
warnings: Monthly LFT monitoring required for riluzole
TSH check in 3 months given levothyroxine co-administration — physiological stress of ALS diagnosis and illness may affect thyroid requirements

output.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/uL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 62 mg/dL. Glucose: 64 mg/dL (ratio 0.69). NfL: 9,280 pg/mL. Oligoclonal bands: Absent.
Abnormal values: ALSFRS-R 32 points (H), ALSFRS-R Bulbar subscale 8 points (H).

ground_truth.primary_diagnosis: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), bulbar-onset, with early respiratory involvement

differential.key_feature: MG causes fatigable weakness without fasciculations, LMN signs, or EMG denervation; AChR antibodies not checked but clinical picture is pure UMN+LMN
Anti-Hu negative; sensory NCS normal (paraneoplastic typically affects sensory > motor); no known malignancy

differential.diagnosis: Primary lateral sclerosis with bulbar involvement
differential.key_feature: PLS is purely UMN — fasciculations, fibrillations, and LMN wasting exclude PLS; 4-region EMG denervation confirms LMN involvement
PBP is a clinical subtype of ALS with predominantly bulbar involvement, but 4-region EMG denervation and bilateral limb Babinski confirm ALS rather than isolated PBP

optimal_actions.action: PFT — early assessment critical in bulbar-onset
optimal_actions.expected_finding: FVC 76%, SNIP 54 — below normal, approaching NIV threshold

optimal_actions.action: Swallowing evaluation — VFSS given dysphagia symptoms
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Thin liquid penetration, recommend thickened liquids

optimal_actions.action: Riluzole — check levothyroxine interaction and TSH monitoring

critical_actions: PFT — urgent given bulbar onset and FVC approaching threshold
PEG placement consultation before FVC falls below 50%
contraindicated_actions: Delaying PEG beyond FVC 50% — PEG placement has unacceptable anesthesia risk below this threshold
key_reasoning_points: Bulbar-onset ALS typically progresses faster than limb-onset — urgent respiratory and nutritional evaluation
PEG tube must be placed while FVC still >50%; current FVC 76% means this window is open but closing
Normal TSH confirms hypothyroid myopathy is NOT contributing — levothyroxine is adequately dosed
Anti-Hu paraneoplastic panel appropriate in female patient with bulbar presentation to exclude paraneoplastic syndrome

metadata.notes: Straightforward bulbar-onset ALS in retired soprano. PEG timing critical given FVC 76%.
